title: CI portability + naming/dead-code cleanups + redact GitHub credentials from error output (v2)
summary: Revision addressing reviewer feedback on the original draft. Five deliverables: (1) pin the bare-remote initial branch in `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py::_init_repo_with_remote` to `main`; (2) drop the dead `RaiseSite` `as`-aliased re-export and its misleading docstring claim in `core/soft_failure.py` (limited surgical edit — do not rewrite the rest of the module docstring); (3) rename `SoftFailureError` → `NoStructuredOutputError` at the class definition, eight raise sites, the `build_error_event` isinstance branch, and every test reference, with no shim and no behavior change; (4) hoist the stderr-tail byte cap from `adapters/claude_client_executor.py` to `core/constants.py` (rationale comment travels with it; rename to `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` per the destination module's uppercase-no-prefix convention — explicitly acknowledged as a justified naming-policy alignment beyond the user's literal request); (5) plug the credential-leak vector — inline a private helper `_redact_credentials(s: str) -> str` and its compiled patterns directly above `build_error_event` in `core/soft_failure.py` (no separate `core/redaction.py` module — two callers, ~10 LOC, YAGNI), define `_REDACTION_SENTINEL: Final[str] = "***REDACTED***"` next to it as the single source of truth shared with tests, apply it in `build_error_event` (both `error` and `stderr_tail` field contents, with None-guards inline at the call sites since the helper takes `str`), and apply it symmetrically in BOTH `claude_client_executor.py:80-90` AND `claude_agent_executor.py:69-73` (structurally identical `awarning("claude_sdk_process_error", ..., stderr=exc.stderr)` calls — the unwired-by-default executor still gets the scrub for future-wired safety, computed once into a local and reused). One inline `# TODO` comment in `chains/ralph_workflow.py::_complete_node` near `merged=state["merged"]` noting a future `reason` field on `WorkflowCompleteEvent`. After this lands `make check` is green including the two previously-failing parametrized divergence cases.
context:
**Branch base**: `kodezart/fix-pipeline-obs-git-remote-is-ancestor-1c5f230d-ralph-27fc4305` @ commit `80aa43d` ("refactor: share build_error_event and dedupe RaiseSite alias"). The observability-widening / git-remote-config / is-ancestor-refspec work is already landed; do not re-open it.

## Why each deliverable

**1. CI portability (fixture pin).** `tests/integration/test_workflow_e2e.py::_init_repo_with_remote` (lines 65-85) pins the working repo via `git init -b main` at line 81 but creates the paired bare via `git init --bare` at line 83 with no initial-branch flag. On a CI host without a global `init.defaultBranch=main`, the bare's HEAD defaults to `master`; a subsequent clone checks out an unborn `master` and `git push <remote> main` fails with `src refspec main does not match any`. Two parametrized cases of `test_git_change_persister_divergence_error_references_configured_remote` (line 718-779, parametrize `remote_name=["origin","upstream"]`) fail in CI while passing locally. Same fix idiom as commit `bccab99` ("test(subprocess_git): pin git_repo fixture initial branch to main"), applied to the bare side.

**2. Dead `RaiseSite` re-export.** `core/soft_failure.py:40-43` carries a comment claiming downstream consumers import `RaiseSite` from this module, which justifies the `from … import RaiseSite as RaiseSite` form (line 51) under mypy strict `no_implicit_reexport`. Repo-wide grep confirms NO consumer imports `RaiseSite` from `core.soft_failure` — every consumer imports `SoftFailureError`, `drain`, or `build_error_event`. `RaiseSite` is used internally in `__init__` and `build_error_event` typed locals only; plain import suffices.

**3. Rename.** `SoftFailureError` reads as a contradiction at raise sites; "soft" describes a retry-severity stance, not the failure mode. The new name `NoStructuredOutputError` names the exact condition every raise site guards on (a missing `ResultEvent`, or a `ResultEvent` whose structured-output payload is absent). Type hierarchy and behavior unchanged.

**4. Hoist `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES`.** The 4096-byte cap is a wire-shape invariant tied to upstream proxy framing (Cloudflare / nginx default `proxy_buffer_size` ~8 KB) — a cross-module workflow constant whose home is `core/constants.py` (peer of `EVAL_PERMISSION_MODE`, `EVAL_TOOLS`, `EVAL_TOOLS_WITH_AGENT`, `TICKET_TOOLS`). The rationale comment must travel verbatim with the constant. The leading-underscore drop (`_STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` → `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES`) is a naming-policy alignment with the destination module's established uppercase-no-prefix convention; it is NOT in the user's literal request but is justified because the constant transitions from module-private to package-shared and the destination convention is unambiguous.

**5. Credential leak (security).** `adapters/github_token_auth.py:10-12` builds `https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/...`. `adapters/subprocess_git_service.py::_run` (line 331-350), `_run_output` (318-329), and `_run_with_exit_codes` (352-384) embed raw stderr — which on fetch/push/clone failure echoes the tokenized URL — into `RuntimeError` messages at lines 327, 349, 379-82. That message becomes `str(exc)` in `core/soft_failure.build_error_event` (line 150) populating `ErrorEvent.error`. Defense-in-depth: `ErrorEvent.stderr_tail` (line 147, AgentSDKError path) and two sibling `awarning("claude_sdk_process_error", stderr=exc.stderr)` calls at `claude_client_executor.py:80-84` and `claude_agent_executor.py:69-73` are structurally identical leak vectors. Scrub at the convergence point (`build_error_event`) plus both adapter log lines. Patterns scoped tightly to the credential URL form and the five published GitHub token prefixes per the deliverable's anti-pattern guard.

**6. TODO comment.** `chains/ralph_workflow.py::_complete_node` (function at line 1029) emits `WorkflowCompleteEvent` with `merged=state["merged"]` at line 1043. Consumers currently must infer "acceptance criteria did not pass" vs "ran but could not merge" from the absence of a consolidation event. Future work: a `reason` field. Comment only.

## Documentation re-verified independently this round

- [git-init(1) — git-scm.com (v2.54.0, dated 2026-04-20)](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init) — synopsis lists `[--bare]` and `[-b <branch-name> | --initial-branch=<branch-name>]` as independent optional flags; the combination is documented with no caveat.
- [Behind GitHub's new authentication token formats — github.blog](https://github.blog/engineering/platform-security/behind-githubs-new-authentication-token-formats/) — taxonomy: `ghp_` (PAT classic), `gho_` (OAuth), `ghu_` (user-to-server), `ghs_` (server-to-server), `ghr_` (refresh); classic body is Base62 with documented length ~36 chars.
- [Managing your personal access tokens — docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens) — fine-grained PATs use the `github_pat_` prefix.
- [Python 3.12.13 `re` module reference — docs.python.org/3.12/library/re.html](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/re.html) — quoted directly: "`\b` is defined as the boundary between a `\w` and a `\W` character (or vice versa)". Since `_` is in `\w`, a trailing `\b` after `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` does NOT fire between `_` and a word char and is effectively a no-op there. Use a non-`\w` lookahead or rely on `+` greediness with a length lower bound.
- [structlog API reference — structlog.org/en/stable/api.html](https://www.structlog.org/en/stable/api.html) — `structlog.testing.capture_logs(processors=())` is a stable context manager, added in structlog 20.1.0; appends every log event-dict to a yielded list and disables configured processors for the duration. structlog is already in `pyproject.toml`. Safe to use unconditionally.
- [Ruff S105 `hardcoded-password-string` — docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/hardcoded-password-string](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/hardcoded-password-string/) — and [ruff issue #8789](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/8789) — confirm S105 triggers on literal string assignments to a variable whose name contains `token` (alongside `password`, `secret`, etc.). The active ruleset selects `S` and tests/** waives only `S101` and `S108` — S105/S106 ARE active in tests. Therefore: test fixtures must NOT use `token = "ghp_..."`-style assignments; construct fixtures via string concatenation or assign to non-credential-named variables (e.g. `fake_url`, `tokenized_url`, `creds_blob`) — see the test-file change descriptions for the exact pattern. NO `# noqa: S105` and NO widening of per-file-ignores — that would violate the project's no-disable-linter policy.

## Layout / lint constraints

`pyproject.toml`: mypy strict + `disallow_any_explicit=true` + `no_implicit_reexport=true`; ruff selects `E,W,F,I,B,C4,UP,N,ANN,S,A,ARG,RUF` (note: `FIX*` and `TD*` are NOT in the selection, so a bare `# TODO:` comment is acceptable and needs no issue-link annotation); pydantic-mypy `init_forbid_extra=true`. Makefile `check` = `verify-no-origin-literal lint type-check test`. The hexagonal-layering rule is `adapters → core` OK, `adapters → chains` forbidden; `core/soft_failure.py` is already legally importable from `adapters/` (the existing `git_change_persister.py:15` import proves it), so inlining the redaction helper there does not introduce any new cross-layer edge — both adapter awarning sites already import from `core/`.

## What changed vs the prior draft (reviewer-driven)

- **Helper home**: dropped the proposed standalone `core/redaction.py` module. The helper inlines directly above `build_error_event` in `core/soft_failure.py` — two callers, ~10 LOC, single-file cohesion with the chokepoint that consumes it. A peer module is YAGNI until a third consumer appears.
- **Helper signature**: dropped the `@overload (str)->str / (None)->None` pair. Single `def _redact_credentials(s: str) -> str` with `None`-guards inline at the two call sites (where an `is not None` check is already idiomatic).
- **Sentinel constant**: introduced `_REDACTION_SENTINEL: Final[str] = "***REDACTED***"` next to the helper. Used as the regex replacement template AND asserted by tests — single source of truth.
- **Regex narrowing**: dropped the `{36,255}` upper bound on both bare patterns. The literal `gh[posu]_` and `github_pat_` prefixes anchor the match; the `[^@\s/]+` body of the URL form is already ReDoS-safe because the surrounding `x-access-token:` and `@` literals bracket it. Keep documented length lower bounds (`{36,}` classic, `{20,}` fine-grained) so short-suffix false positives are avoided. Inline comment cites the official prefix taxonomy.
- **Parallel leak vector**: redact in BOTH `claude_client_executor.py:80-90` AND `claude_agent_executor.py:69-73`. Compute the redacted stderr once into a local in each adapter and feed BOTH the `awarning(..., stderr=...)` kwarg AND (in the client executor only — the agent executor doesn't slice) the `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` slice from the same local. Test coverage is limited to the wired (client) executor per the existing in-file TODO at `claude_agent_executor.py:56-63` which justifies CI-cost economy on the unwired one; the redaction call itself is symmetric.
- **`core/soft_failure.py` docstring change scope**: limited to (a) removing the inaccurate `RaiseSite` re-export claim and (b) updating the in-text `SoftFailureError` references to `NoStructuredOutputError`. The rest of the docstring (peer-of-AgentSDKError positioning, primitive-only invariant, `core/` layering rationale) is unchanged — do not rewrite.
- **Open Questions resolved into the design**: (1) placeholder is `***REDACTED***` (user-prescribed); (2) `structlog.testing.capture_logs()` is the testing mechanism (stable API since 20.1.0); (3) the new `core/soft_failure.py` test exercises a single representative `RaiseSite` literal — the eight literals are already covered at their actual raise sites in the chain-level tests, exhaustive duplication is wasteful.
- **Reference correction**: `_STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` is at line 26 of `claude_client_executor.py`; lines 21-25 are the rationale comment block (the prior draft said "21-26" for both).
- **PR-description note (not a code change)**: the leak ORIGIN is `subprocess_git_service.py` `_run*` methods at lines 327, 349, 379-82, which `f"{...} failed: {stderr.decode().strip()}"` raw stderr into `RuntimeError`. The user's design explicitly chooses egress-point (convergence) redaction; source-side redaction would reshape the adapter's exception construction in a way the design rejects. Call this out in the PR body so a follow-up author understands the choke point is downstream of the leak.

requiredChanges.description:
Multi-part edit, all in this file:

(1) **Surgical docstring trim** (lines 1-36): delete ONLY the sentence(s) claiming downstream consumers import `RaiseSite` from this module (the inaccurate claim around lines 8-11), and replace every in-text occurrence of `SoftFailureError` with `NoStructuredOutputError`. Do NOT rewrite the rest — the peer-of-AgentSDKError positioning, the primitive-only invariant, the `core/` layering rationale, and the explanation of why `drain` is a coroutine all stay verbatim.

(2) **Drop the dead re-export** (lines 40-43 and 51): delete the comment block at 40-43 and replace line 51 `from kodezart.types.domain.agent import RaiseSite as RaiseSite` with a plain `RaiseSite` folded into the existing multi-import block from `kodezart.types.domain.agent` (which already imports `AgentEvent`, `ErrorEvent`, `RateLimitWarningEvent`, `ResultEvent`).

(3) **Rename the class** (line 54): `class SoftFailureError(Exception):` → `class NoStructuredOutputError(Exception):`. Update the class docstring's references to the old name. Constructor signature, attribute storage, peer-of-AgentSDKError hierarchy — unchanged. Update the isinstance check in `build_error_event` (line 141) to match.

(4) **Add redaction primitives** immediately ABOVE `build_error_event` (between line 119 and 121), in this exact shape (private to the module, no separate file):

```python
from typing import Final

# GitHub token taxonomy (prefixes per the published format spec):
#   ghp_ classic PAT, gho_ OAuth, ghu_ user-to-server, ghs_ server-to-server
#   github_pat_ fine-grained PAT.
# Body lower-bounds anchor on documented lengths so short-suffix prose
# matches (e.g. "ghp_abc") are not scrubbed.  No upper bound — the literal
# prefix anchors prevent runaway backtracking.
_REDACTION_SENTINEL: Final[str] = "***REDACTED***"
_CREDENTIAL_URL_PATTERN: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(
    r"(https?://x-access-token:)[^@\s/]+(@)"
)
_GH_TOKEN_PATTERN: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(r"\bgh[posu]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}")
_GH_FINEGRAINED_PAT_PATTERN: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(
    r"\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}"
)


def _redact_credentials(s: str) -> str:
    """Replace GitHub credential patterns with the redaction sentinel.

    Applied at the two ErrorEvent egress fields below and at both
    Claude-SDK adapter ``claude_sdk_process_error`` log calls.  Patterns
    are tightly scoped to the credential URL form and the five published
    GitHub token prefixes — wider matches risk scrubbing non-secret
    operator text, which the ticket explicitly forbids.
    """
    s = _CREDENTIAL_URL_PATTERN.sub(rf"\1{_REDACTION_SENTINEL}\2", s)
    s = _GH_TOKEN_PATTERN.sub(_REDACTION_SENTINEL, s)
    s = _GH_FINEGRAINED_PAT_PATTERN.sub(_REDACTION_SENTINEL, s)
    return s
```

Add `import re` next to the existing `from collections.abc import AsyncIterator` (top of file).

(5) **Apply redaction in `build_error_event`** (lines 149-158): change the returned `ErrorEvent(...)` to redact both leak-carrying fields. `str(exc)` is unconditionally a `str`, so feed it directly. `stderr_tail` is `str | None`, so use an inline None-guard at the call site (matches the existing idiom in this function):

```python
return ErrorEvent(
    error=_redact_credentials(str(exc)),
    error_kind=error_kind,
    cause_class=cause_class,
    stop_reason=stop_reason,
    raise_site=raise_site,
    rate_limit_rejected=rate_limit_rejected,
    exit_code=exit_code,
    stderr_tail=(
        _redact_credentials(stderr_tail) if stderr_tail is not None else None
    ),
)
```
requiredChanges.rationale: Deliverables 2, 3, and 5 converge on this single file. The helper, sentinel, and patterns live here (NOT in a separate `core/redaction.py` module — two callers, ~10 LOC, YAGNI per the reviewer's architecture note). Inlining keeps single-file cohesion with `build_error_event`, the chokepoint that consumes the helper. The cross-module adapter import of `_redact_credentials` is acceptable Python (leading underscore is a convention, not an enforced visibility); the `_validate_permission_mode` import from `adapters/_permission_modes.py` is precedent in this codebase. A single `(str) -> str` signature beats the `@overload` pair because both call sites already have an `is not None` check available. The class rename + isinstance-branch update is mechanical; the docstring change is surgical (do not rewrite the rest).

requiredChanges.description:
Multi-part edit inside the `except ProcessError as exc:` block (lines 79-96), plus the constant move.

(1) **Remove lines 21-26** (the rationale-comment lines 21-25 + the `_STDERR_TAIL_BYTES: int = 4096` assignment on line 26).

(2) **Add two core imports** next to the existing `from kodezart.core.logging import BoundLogger, get_logger`:
```python
from kodezart.core.constants import STDERR_TAIL_BYTES
from kodezart.core.soft_failure import _redact_credentials
```

(3) **Compute redaction once into a local, feed both downstream uses**. Replace the existing block lines 79-96 with the following structure (preserving every other line verbatim):
```python
except ProcessError as exc:
    stderr_redacted: str | None = (
        _redact_credentials(exc.stderr) if exc.stderr is not None else None
    )
    await self._log.awarning(
        "claude_sdk_process_error",
        exit_code=exc.exit_code,
        stderr=stderr_redacted,
    )
    stderr_tail: str | None = (
        stderr_redacted[:STDERR_TAIL_BYTES] if stderr_redacted is not None else None
    )
    raise AgentSDKError(
        str(exc),
        error_kind="ProcessError",
        exit_code=exc.exit_code,
        stderr_tail=stderr_tail,
    ) from exc
```

The `CLIConnectionError` and `ClaudeSDKError` branches (lines 97-114) are untouched — their `awarning` calls log `error=str(exc)`, NOT raw `exc.stderr`, and `AgentSDKError(str(exc), ...)` for those branches is scrubbed downstream by `build_error_event`'s `error=_redact_credentials(str(exc))`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Deliverable 4 (hoist) + deliverable 5 (redact). Computing the redacted string ONCE into a local and feeding both the `awarning(..., stderr=...)` kwarg AND the `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` slice from the same local: (a) avoids running the regex twice on the same payload, (b) guarantees the two emissions are byte-identical with respect to redaction, and (c) eliminates the truncation-boundary leak where a token straddling the 4096-byte slice could otherwise survive partially exposed in `AgentSDKError.stderr_tail` only. The `if exc.stderr is not None` guard is already idiomatic here — no `@overload`-pair plumbing required.

requiredChanges.description:
Symmetric redaction in the parallel `awarning` call. Inside the `except ProcessError as exc:` block (lines 68-77):

(1) **Add the same import** next to the existing `from kodezart.core.logging import BoundLogger, get_logger`:
```python
from kodezart.core.soft_failure import _redact_credentials
```

(2) **Replace the `awarning` call** (lines 69-73) to redact the `stderr` kwarg:
```python
await self._log.awarning(
    "claude_sdk_process_error",
    exit_code=exc.exit_code,
    stderr=_redact_credentials(exc.stderr) if exc.stderr is not None else None,
)
```

Do NOT introduce a `stderr_tail` slice here — this executor's `raise AgentSDKError(str(exc), error_kind="ProcessError")` (lines 74-77) does NOT populate `exit_code` / `stderr_tail` and the file's existing in-line TODO at lines 56-63 explicitly defers that detail-preservation work as out-of-scope for an unwired code path. The `str(exc)` flowing into `AgentSDKError.__str__` is downstream-scrubbed by `build_error_event`'s `error=_redact_credentials(str(exc))`.

The `CLIConnectionError` and `ClaudeSDKError` branches (lines 78-95) are untouched for the same reason as in `claude_client_executor.py`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Deliverable 5, symmetric leak-vector fix. The reviewer correctly identified this as a structurally identical `awarning("claude_sdk_process_error", stderr=exc.stderr)` call. The redaction call itself is 1 LOC and free; the asymmetry (redacting one adapter and leaving the other raw) would introduce a latent bug the moment the agent executor gets wired. The existing in-file TODO at lines 56-63 acknowledges this executor is currently unwired in the default composition root — hence no new test for THIS file (CI cost-economy argument from the existing TODO applies), but the redaction itself is symmetric.

requiredChanges.description:
New test module for `core/soft_failure.py` (no current home; `tests/core/test_retry.py` tests `should_retry`, NOT `build_error_event` / redaction). Imports both the renamed `NoStructuredOutputError` and the redaction sentinel via `from kodezart.core.soft_failure import NoStructuredOutputError, _REDACTION_SENTINEL, _redact_credentials, build_error_event`. Imports `AgentSDKError` from `kodezart.domain.errors`.

**Fixture-naming policy** (avoids ruff S105/S106 trigger — the active ruleset selects `S` and tests/** waives only `S101`/`S108`; `S105`/`S106` ARE active in tests, and they trigger on `token = "<literal>"` because "token" is in the rule's password-keyword list per the official ruff docs). Construct token fixtures via concatenation, NOT as a literal assignment to a token-named variable. Use names like `creds_url`, `tokenized_url`, `fake_url`, `gh_body`, `pat_body`. Example shape:

```python
_FAKE_GHP_BODY: Final[str] = "A" * 40  # name does not match S105 keyword list
_FAKE_URL: Final[str] = (
    f"https://x-access-token:ghp_{_FAKE_GHP_BODY}@github.com/o/r.git"
)
```

**Tests** (six total):

1. `test_redact_credentials_redacts_embedded_url_token` — call `_redact_credentials(_FAKE_URL)`; assert the literal `_FAKE_GHP_BODY` string is absent from the result, that the result contains `https://x-access-token:` and `@github.com/o/r.git` (scheme + sentinel + suffix preserved), and that the result contains `_REDACTION_SENTINEL`.

2. `test_redact_credentials_redacts_bare_classic_tokens` — parametrize over `prefix in ["ghp_", "gho_", "ghs_", "ghu_"]`; for each, build `f"prefix line: {prefix}{'A' * 40} trailing"` and assert the suffix portion is replaced with `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` while `prefix line:` and `trailing` survive.

3. `test_redact_credentials_redacts_fine_grained_pat` — build `f"github_pat_{'B' * 22}_{'C' * 59}"`; assert the whole token is replaced with `_REDACTION_SENTINEL`.

4. `test_redact_credentials_preserves_non_secret_text` — inputs `"hello world"`, `"feature/ghp-thing"` (branch name), `"ghp_short"` (3-char suffix below the 36-char floor); assert each is returned unchanged.

5. `test_redact_credentials_is_idempotent` — `_redact_credentials(_redact_credentials(_FAKE_URL)) == _redact_credentials(_FAKE_URL)`.

6. `test_build_error_event_redacts_token_in_error_field` — raise a `RuntimeError(f"git push failed: remote: {_FAKE_URL}")` and `try/except` to capture it; call `build_error_event(exc)`; assert `_FAKE_GHP_BODY` is NOT in `event.error` and `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` IS in `event.error`.

7. `test_build_error_event_redacts_token_in_stderr_tail_field` — construct `AgentSDKError("process failed", error_kind="ProcessError", exit_code=128, stderr_tail=_FAKE_URL)`; call`build_error_event(exc)`; assert `_FAKE_GHP_BODY` is NOT in `event.stderr_tail` and `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` IS.

8. `test_build_error_event_no_structured_output_carries_raise_site` — single representative literal (`raise_site="branch_name"`) is sufficient; chain-level tests already exercise each `RaiseSite` literal at its actual raise site. Assert `event.raise_site == "branch_name"`, `event.rate_limit_rejected is False`, `event.error_kind == "NoStructuredOutputError"` (smoke test for the rename + the build_error_event isinstance branch).

9. `test_build_error_event_preserves_non_secret_message` — `event = build_error_event(ValueError("plain operator text"))`; assert `event.error == "plain operator text"`.
requiredChanges.rationale: Deliverable 5d. The reviewer resolved Open Question 3: single representative `RaiseSite` is sufficient. The fixture-naming policy avoids ruff S105 trigger without disabling the linter — the no-disable-linter project rule is honored. Importing the private `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` / `_redact_credentials` from within the same package is acceptable Python (leading underscore is convention only) and gives the tests a single source of truth for the placeholder string.

requiredChanges.description:
Add two tests to the existing `ClaudeClientExecutor` test block. Test ONLY `ClaudeClientExecutor` — the parallel `ClaudeAgentExecutor` redaction is symmetric but not exercised by tests, consistent with the existing in-file TODO at `claude_agent_executor.py:56-63` arguing CI-cost economy on an unwired code path.

**Fixture-naming policy**: same as in `test_soft_failure.py` — construct token fixtures via concatenation (not literal assignment to a token-named variable) to dodge ruff S105.

**Test 1** — `test_process_error_redacts_token_in_warning_log`:
- Build `creds_url = f"https://x-access-token:ghp_{'A' * 40}@github.com/o/r.git"`.
- Patch the SDK client so its `query()` raises `ProcessError(message=f"git fetch failed: {creds_url} permission denied", exit_code=128, stderr=creds_url)`.
- Wrap the executor `stream()` drain inside `structlog.testing.capture_logs() as captured:` (stable structlog API since 20.1.0 — verified during planning).
- After the `pytest.raises(AgentSDKError)`, assert: (i) at least one captured event has `event == "claude_sdk_process_error"` and `"stderr" in event`; (ii) that record's `stderr` value equals `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` substring at the location where `ghp_AAAA…` would otherwise appear AND the literal `"A" * 40` body string is NOT in `stderr`; (iii) the literal 40-char body does NOT appear anywhere in any captured record's serialized form.
- Import `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` from `kodezart.core.soft_failure` for the assertion (single source of truth).

**Test 2** — `test_process_error_stderr_tail_on_agent_sdk_error_is_redacted`:
- Same `ProcessError` setup.
- Drain the executor inside `pytest.raises(AgentSDKError) as excinfo:`.
- Assert: `excinfo.value.stderr_tail is not None`, the literal `"A" * 40` body is NOT in `excinfo.value.stderr_tail`, and `_REDACTION_SENTINEL` IS in `excinfo.value.stderr_tail`. This covers the redact-before-slice ordering: a token straddling the 4096-byte boundary cannot survive partially exposed.

Both tests use the existing `_FakeSDKClient` pattern at the top of this file (lines 59-77) — reuse it; do not introduce a parallel fake.
requiredChanges.rationale: Deliverable 5d. `structlog.testing.capture_logs()` is the stable, official testing entry point (added in structlog 20.1.0, re-verified against current docs this round). Single-source-of-truth sentinel import means a future placeholder change updates one constant and both tests follow. NO `S105/S106` waivers — fixture construction via concatenation works under the active rule selection.

Other `error=str(exc)` log sites in `adapters/git_worktree_provider.py`, `adapters/git_branch_merger.py`, `adapters/git_artifact_persister.py` — same leak family but downstream of `str(exc)` which is already scrubbed by `build_error_event`; the user's deliverable names the two `awarning(..., stderr=exc.stderr)` log calls specifically.

Adding test coverage for the redaction in `claude_agent_executor.py` — the executor is unwired by default per the in-file TODO at lines 56-63; the redaction is applied for future-wired safety but not separately tested, consistent with that file's existing CI-cost-economy argument.
`.netrc`, `Authorization:` HTTP headers, or other credential surfaces beyond the `x-access-token` URL and the five named GitHub token prefixes.
Pre/post test hooks, conftest fixtures, or CI lifecycle changes to mask the divergence-test CI failure — fix is solely the bare-repo `-b main` pin.
A global structlog processor that scrubs every event-dict value — widens scope past the deliverable; call-site redaction only at the two named log lines.
Any backwards-compatibility alias (`SoftFailureError = NoStructuredOutputError`) — anti-pattern; rename leaves no shim.
A standalone `core/redaction.py` module — the prior draft proposed one; the inline helper in `core/soft_failure.py` satisfies the requirement with strictly less code and tighter cohesion.
